class: A reviewer demands a walk of a new plan while the legacy framework's coarse conclusions stay the same; the review must re-key on the new demand, and a receipt for the old demand must not satisfy it.

inputs.demand_key_assumption: demand.key = H(plan_sha256, subject); requested_by (the requesting review) is not part of it

notes: Order: (1) the internal/receipt applicability verdict when walk-1790943778… (old plan) is offered for the new demand: inapplicable (registered); in the graph this is a structural waiting(input), never a cached or retried node result; (2) the new demand gets its own evidence attempt, walk-1790945582… (24 steps against 18); (3) the successor review's key changes: in auto-dev-cycle terms the conclusions differ too (note 06 conclusions_digest includes the demand key and per-step outcomes), only the legacy coarse conclusions were equal; (4) counter-case: walk-1790902623… and walk-1790943778… walk the same plan with equal conclusions, so no re-review. Step 4 holds only under the demand_key_assumption and only if the grant rebind between those walks (different grant digests) changed none of subject, demand, instrument digest or restrictions; both are open points for the vocabulary PR (README).
